conviction_note: The lean is up and mild (p_up 56 on a 9% absolute move, giving +1.08). The stock gapped down 23% on 2026-11-12 with no company filing, sits at its 52-week low with short interest rising, and the Q3 revenue consensus is in the lower half of a guide the company has hit at or above the midpoint. Against that, the reaction turns on the Q4 guide, and last year's Q4 guide set marginally below FactSet sold off about 6%. The AI-replaces-hiring narrative behind the sector sell-off will not be settled by one print, so p_up stays near 50. impact_sum (+1.7) is larger than the scaled number because the positioning and expectations findings each carry their own size, while the sign uncertainty sits in p_up.

next_guide.basis: Q2 accelerated to +14.1% and the Q3 guide midpoint is +13.5%. October urban unemployment fell to a four-month low of 5.1% and the youth rate fell to 17.2%. October manufacturing PMI employment was flat at 48.4. Together these point to a Q4 guide of roughly 11-14%, near the street, not a cut. Last year's Q4 guide, however, was set marginally below consensus.

findings.finding: BZ gapped down 23% on 2026-11-12, from $16.72 to an open of $13.95, with no company filing (MarketBeat). Press attributed the fall to a China/AI tech sell-off (Golden Dragon index -3%, BABA -7%) and to unverified 'softer guidance' chatter. The stock has since drifted to $12.55, a 52-week low and 46% below the $18.33 mean target. The 13.2% Q2 growth and 13.5% Q3 guide midpoint have not been contradicted by any company statement since 2026-08-25.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a pre-print sell-off into Q2 2026 (stock about $14-16), an in-line print plus capital return bought +5.5% on the day and more than 20% over two days.
findings.why_not_priced: The 23% gap priced a guidance disappointment that no document has confirmed. If the rumour were already fully reflected, the sector's 3% fall would not leave BZ 20 points behind it. Equally, the price would have retraced if the market saw the rumour as baseless, and it has not: the stock sits at the low. Either the guide confirms the rumour (little further downside) or it does not (a sharp retrace).
findings.independence: 10jqka (2026-11-13, https://stock.10jqka.com.cn/20261113/c681791793.shtml) gives the same date and the sector/AI cause and notes fundamentals unchanged. KoalaGains (https://koalagains.com/daily-top-movers/top-losers/details/9ee80948-0b07-40db-bf7d-832daddc9bfe) cites unverified guidance chatter. Both describe the same price event.

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 24.26M shares (2026-09-30) to 28.23M (2026-10-15) to 30.22M (2026-10-30), about 6.9% of 437.5M shares outstanding. Days to cover went from 3.6 to 7.5. Shorts built into the crash, and a guide that is merely in line forces covering against 7.5 days of volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a +5.5% day became more than +20% over two days, consistent with short covering, though short interest at that print was not found (24.1M at the 2026-08-14 settlement per curvedtrading).
findings.why_not_priced: The 2026-11-13 settlement is unpublished, so how many shorts covered during the crash is not visible. Call-heavy OI (put/call 0.23) suggests upside convexity is held, not a crowded put book.
findings.independence: Benzinga/curvedtrading show 24.1M at 2026-08-14 with DTC 7.4 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/bz/short-interest/), a different data window, same direction of a sizeable short base. One data vendor family.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue consensus is $362.7M (EW) to $363.2M (Benzinga), about RMB2.44bn and +12.7% y/y, below the RMB2.455bn guide midpoint. The company landed mid-range in Q2 2026 (RMB2,398.6m on a RMB2.38-2.42bn guide) and above the top in Q3 2025 (RMB2,163.3m). A print of RMB2.45-2.48bn would beat consensus by about 0.5-1.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats or in-line prints were sold in Q1 2025 (-7% intraday) and Q3 2025 (-6% pre-market on the Q4 guide). Benzinga shows revenue landing slightly below the USD consensus four quarters running while EPS beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a print inside the company's own range is the base case. The only unpriced part is that consensus sits below the midpoint the company has reached.
findings.independence: Company guide in the Q2 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001842827/000110465926100537/tm2623958d1_ex99-1.htm). Q2 2026 guide range from Nasdaq/Quartr summaries (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/kanzhun-q1-earnings-call-highlights).

findings.finding: The Q4 guide decides the reaction, and this company sets it conservatively. The Q4 2025 guide (RMB2.05-2.07bn) sat marginally below FactSet's RMB2.07bn and the stock fell 5.7-6.7% pre-market on a Q3 beat. Street Q4 2026 is $346.5M, about RMB2.33bn or roughly +12% y/y. The Q3 2026 guide range was unusually wide (RMB90m against RMB40m for Q2), which signals management uncertainty about H2 demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: Q4 guide fractionally below consensus gave -5.7% to -6.7% pre-market (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1167059282). Q2 2026: a Q3 guide whose midpoint was near consensus, plus the dividend, gave +5.5% and then more than 20% over two days.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 2026-11-12 crash discounts a soft guide. Not priced: the company's habit of guiding to or a hair below the street, which against a de-rated stock makes 'slightly below' less damaging than last year. Net, it stays a modest negative because the habit is real.
findings.independence: Street Q4 figure is a Benzinga snippet (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BZ/earnings-forecasts). Q3 guide width is from the Q2 6-K. Different documents.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 sales and marketing rose 38.3% to RMB580.9m on a one-off FIFA World Cup campaign, yet adjusted operating margin still reached a record 43.8%. Management guided Q3 margins similar to Q2, so with the World Cup spend gone Q3 adjusted operating income has room above the $0.27-0.29 EPS consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beat four quarters running (Benzinga snippet), with reactions dominated by revenue and the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The EPS consensus ($0.27) is flat on Q2's $0.27 despite the removal of a one-off marketing cost. If the market modelled the reversal, consensus would sit above Q2.
findings.independence: Q3 margin guidance 'similar to Q2' is from a search summary of the call. The 43.8% margin is from the EW preview (https://finviz.com/news/424951/kanzhuns-pricing-pivot-faces-first-real-test-as-shares-slide-toward-range-lows).

findings.finding: Buybacks reached about RMB2.06bn in H1 2026 (last release found 2026-07-01) against a US$400M (RMB2.9bn) authorization running to 2027-08-28, leaving roughly US$100-120M. No repurchase release was found for the 2026-11-12 crash. The company has committed to return at least 50% of prior-year adjusted net income each year for three years, already exceeded 100% for 2026, and may announce a new or upsized programme with the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 release carried a $230M dividend; the stock rose 5.5% on the day and more than 20% over two days.
findings.why_not_priced: A new authorization is not announced, and the stock trades around 9x earnings (MarketBeat P/E 9.02). Whether the company uses a de-rated price is not visible until the release.
findings.independence: The Paper 2026-04-12 (https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32948260) gives the RMB2.9bn authorization and the three-year 50% payout pledge.

findings.finding: Insider sales in September 2026: the CMO sold 400,000 shares (2026-09-09, about $3.4M) and the CEO 743,600 shares (2026-09-14, about $6.12M). This follows the CEO's earlier HK$863M block sale, reportedly for an offshore tax bill.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. It has been public since September and is small against the market cap of about $5.3bn.
findings.independence: Benzinga CMO sale (https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/09/61717650). The sales' dollar values are inconsistent with quoted prices, so treat them as indicative.

findings.finding: October 2026 China labour data: urban surveyed unemployment fell to 5.1% (four-month low, -0.1pt m/m) and the 16-24 youth rate to 17.2% from 18.0%. The October NBS manufacturing PMI employment index was 48.4 (flat) and non-manufacturing 46.0 (+0.1). Hiring demand into Q4 looks stable, not deteriorating.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy: macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed. The 2026-11-12 sell-off narrative of 'pessimistic job-market expectations' runs against these prints.
findings.independence: Unemployment: Bastille Post (https://www.bastillepost.com/global/article/6363499-chinas-surveyed-urban-unemployment-rate-falls-to-5-1-pct-in-october). Youth rate: World Journal / TrendForce. These are separate from the PMI release.

findings.finding: Recruit Holdings (reported 2026-11-11) grew HR Technology revenue 27.5% y/y (US +36.6%), yet its shares fell 1.4% and 5.6% on 11 and 12 November. SEEK is down about 45% over the year. Online-recruitment platforms are being de-rated on AI-hiring fear regardless of their prints.
findings.link: Same business model (online recruitment marketplace monetised by employer fees); no shared customers or geography. Recruit's HR Tech is US/Japan-weighted, BZ is 100% China.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It shows the AI narrative can overpower good fundamentals, which cuts both ways for BZ: a strong print may still be faded.
findings.independence: same article as finding 1; none further

findings.finding: Inside the quarter the company made only operational and marketing statements: a 2026-09-17 Shenzhen open day on AI job roles and a 2026-09-18 to 22 cloud job fair (5.2M visits, 500k conversations). No reaffirmation, pre-release or guidance comment was found after the 2026-08-25 call.
findings.why_not_priced: These are promotional platform figures with no y/y base and little signal. Filed for completeness.

findings.finding: GAAP earnings in Q1 and Q2 2026 were inflated by fair-value gains on an investee that listed in Q1 2026 (RMB614.1m in Q1, RMB1,466.1m pre-tax in Q2, excluded from adjusted net income). Q3 GAAP EPS will swing with that investee's Q3 share price, which explains GAAP EPS estimates diverging from adjusted ones. This is a below-operating-income item with no path to the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 net income +173% from this gain; the reaction was driven by revenue, the guide and the dividend.
findings.why_not_priced: The market looks through it to adjusted figures. A GAAP 'miss' headline could cause a brief pre-market wobble only.

findings.finding: Analysts cut targets after the crash. Barclays went from $20 to $17 on 2026-11-13 (Overweight kept). The search also reported Citi from $26 to $22, unverified. The consensus rating is Hold (2 Buy, 3 Hold) with a mean target of $18.33.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced. The cuts follow the price; they do not lead it.

baseline_tension: The findings lean against the 20-day run-up: the -24.6% run-up reads as a crash on unconfirmed rumour, and the lean is up. The baseline carries no skew to fight, and call-heavy OI does not argue for puts. The AI-disruption narrative and last year's sold Q4 guide keep p_up close to 50.

Lesson 7 (positioning is a mechanism, not a thesis): short-build finding trimmed from +0.8 to +0.6; DTC 7.5 is moderate, not 18-23% of float.
Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): consensus-bar beat trimmed from +0.3 to +0.2 because this name sold in-line beats in Q1 2025 and Q3 2025.
